title: From the Moon to the time on your clock

lessons.objective: Turn a model Earth and follow a place from light into darkness.
Picture a ball beside a lamp to understand the Moon’s changing face.
See how Earth’s little lean changes the sunlight we get.
Follow three clocks to understand why places use different times.
Distinguish solar and lunar eclipses by alignment, shadow and Moon phase.
Explain synchronous rotation, distinguish the far side from darkness and recognise the small change in viewpoint called libration.

glossary.definition: One of the different views we get of the Moon’s bright side.
An area that follows the same rules for its clocks.
An alignment where one object blocks sunlight from reaching another object or from reaching our view.
One turn on an object’s axis in the same time as one orbit around its partner.
Small apparent rocking of the Moon that changes our view around its edges.

outcomes: Connect day and night to Earth’s rotation.
Explain lunar phases without confusing them with eclipses.
Connect seasons to tilt, sunlight angle and daylight.
Distinguish a time zone from its current UTC offset.
Distinguish solar and lunar eclipses by alignment, shadow and Moon phase.
Explain why the Moon rotates while keeping roughly the same side facing Earth, and why its far side is not always dark.
description: Explore day and night, Moon phases, seasons, time zones and eclipses, then discover why the Moon keeps its familiar face towards Earth.
introduction:
A ball beside a lamp, the changing evening light and a call to a faraway friend help us make sense of the sky and our clocks.

Follow the light through phases and eclipses, then picture a walk around a chair to understand the Moon’s hidden turn. Read at your own pace; the quizzes are optional.
prerequisites: No astronomy background needed. The time-zone lesson includes simple clock arithmetic.
